transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (Redwood PM) - Maya Lopez (AuroraCloud PM), Ethan Brooks (Integration Eng), Sara Ahmed (Marketplace Ops)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on AuroraCloud marketplace listing requirements, finalize reference architecture for joint solution (hosted + private options), and agree on next steps for integration artifacts and smoke tests. Some discussion on SSO, KMS and network/topology constraints.

[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we've got about 54 minutes on the calendar, quick intros?
[00:10] Maya Lopez: hi hi Maya here, Partner PM at AuroraCloud, thanks Liam, excited to get this moving
[00:16] Ethan Brooks: Ethan, integrations eng, I'll be hands on for the testing side
[00:19] Sara Ahmed: Sara, I run marketplace ops, will need final assets and legal pointers
[00:23] Priya Rao: Priya from Redwood SE, I'll lead the reference arch and infra questions
[00:27] Jordan Miles: Jordan - product, here to align on listing copy and joint solution positioning

[02:30] Liam Chen: quick agenda — 1) marketplace listing fields & assets, 2) reference architecture (hosted, dedicated, private/VPC) 3) integration checklist (SSO, KMS, audit logs) 4) next steps. Any additions?
[02:45] Maya Lopez: sounds good, also timeline for going live on the Aurora marketplace, we were thinking early May if nothing blocks us

[07:15] Priya Rao: on the ref arch — Redwood provides a reference architecture that covers three patterns: hosted (Redwood hosted API), dedicated (reserved GPU pool via Redwood Dedicated), and private (VPC or on-prem). For Aurora we should capture the VPC peering option, and an option for customer-managed KMS/HSM for key control.
[07:40] Ethan Brooks: for private deployment, can you share what manifests/artifacts you provide? like helm charts, terraform modules?
[07:50] Priya Rao: yes we have terraform snippets and helm charts; I'll attach a small terraform module that shows the networking (subnets, SGs, endpoints). note: our exported snippets are light, not full infra-as-code but enough to be a pattern.
[08:10] Ethan Brooks: perfect, that will help with our security review

[15:05] Maya Lopez: marketplace ops — what fields do you need? Some marketplaces want pricing tiers, images, console screenshots, integration docs, support SLAs
[15:20] Jordan Miles: we need logo (svg + png), 2 screenshots of console flows (deploy-flow, model selection), short & long descriptions, support contact, and recommended pricing bands (hosted / dedicated / private). we'll draft pricing suggestions but want Aurora to confirm acceptable marketplace revenue share, etc.
[15:45] Sara Ahmed: on our side we need a legal contact and a compliance checklist: SOC 2, ISO, data residency statements. do you have a compliance pack?
[15:58] Priya Rao: yes we have a security pack (SOC 2 Type II summary, encryption at rest/in transit docs, KMS integration notes). I'll share a redacted copy; full artifacts need NDA/secure transfer.

[28:40] Liam Chen: architecture specifics: for private deployments — typical pattern is customer deploys the Redwood private control plane in their VPC, we provide images and helm chart, customer can opt for KMS integration (customer-managed key) and VPC peering or Transit Gateway. There was earlier mention of KV cache — sorry K V cache — for latency we recommend colocating cache in same AZ.
[28:55] Ethan Brooks: when you say 'private control plane', does that require open inbound rules? we prefer minimal exposure, prefer egress-only connections from our VPC to Redwood endpoints
[29:10] Priya Rao: good Q, private control plane can be configured for egress-only using a NAT+S3/private endpoints for updates, and you can run the inference workers in a private subnet. There is a management plane that needs access for telemetry but telemetry can be queued to your logging endpoint if you want, or we can disable telemetry and ship logs via our agent.
[29:35] Maya Lopez: any requirements for IAM roles?
[29:40] Priya Rao: minimum roles: s3 read/write for model artifact pulls, kms:Decrypt for key access (if using KMS), and logs:Put for CloudWatch/Stackdriver equivalent. we'll put a sample IAM role in the terraform snippet.

[42:12] Ethan Brooks: benchmarks — we want a quick compatibility run to check latency and memory profiles for our most common inference workload; can Redwood run on Aurora GPUs?
[42:25] Priya Rao: yes Redwood runtime supports standard NVIDIA A100/A10 and newer chips; however quantization and kernel selection matters. For a smoke test we'll run your model on an equivalent instance. we'll need sample model weights or a public model config; if you provide a representative model or a sim workload we can run in about 48 hours.
[42:55] Liam Chen: note that in marketplace listing we usually call out verified performance for a model+HW combo — we can include a small benchmark table: p50 latency, tokens/sec, cost estimate per 1M tokens.

[50:30] Sara Ahmed: for marketplace publication workflow: we need the listing assets, a security questionnaire answered, and a signed partner agreement. who owns the listing copy?
[50:42] Jordan Miles: Redwood will draft an initial listing copy and pricing tiers; Sara will review and request edits. final signoff by Aurora PM. Typical timeline from assets to publish is 2-3 weeks depending on legal reviews.

[53:00] Maya Lopez: ok timeline looks doable for early May but we'll prioritise providing diagrams this week
[53:10] Liam Chen: recap — Redwood: send marketplace draft, terraform snippets, security pack; Aurora: send network diagram, IAM roles, sample workload for benchmark; both: schedule follow-up demo week of 4/13.
[53:30] Ethan Brooks: one last Q — any redwood limitations on model size for private installs?
[53:40] Priya Rao: no hard limits, mostly depends on GPU memory and quantization. we'll surface recommendations in the reference arch doc.
[53:45] Liam Chen: great thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts and action items in the next 48-72 hours

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., 'K V cash' instead of KV cache, 'redwood dediated' mis-placed words), filler words omitted in places, and some speaker attribution may be generic.
